title: Same Salary. 10 Years Later, One Has $126,766.
description:
Jay and Sam started the same job, on the same day, for the same salary. Ten years later, one of them has $126,766. The other is standing at his door at midnight, asking for help. It came down to one little box on one boring form. A money story about friendship, car payments, credit cards, a layoff, a wedding... and the red SELL button.

0:00 Midnight, 2026
0:39 2016: the boring form
1:50 The red car
3:00 Living for the likes
4:38 2020: the red button
5:41 The couch
6:47 Raises and rings
8:00 The ask
8:55 The best man

The real numbers behind the story:
- Sam puts 6% of a $60,000 salary ($300/month) into his 401(k); the company adds half ($150/month). Invested in the S&P 500 with dividends from Feb 2016 to Nov 2026 (paused Apr-Aug 2020 while laid off): $37,500 of his money + $18,750 free match = $126,766 (before fees and taxes). The free match alone grew to $42,255.
- March 23, 2020: the account fell to $20,730 from about $30,816 in February.
- Jay's $40,000 car at the 2017 average new-car loan rate (4.6%), 72 months: $637/month, $5,864 interest.
- A $6,000 card balance at today's average card rate (22.36%), paying only the minimum (interest + 1%): 20.8 years and $10,105 in interest.

Are you Jay or Sam? Tell me in one word.

Data: S&P 500 Total Return index (Yahoo Finance ^SP500TR); Federal Reserve G.19 via FRED (TERMCBCCINTNS card APR, TERMCBAUTO48NS new-car loan rate).

Jay, Sam and their choices are made up; the rates and market returns are real. Past results don't promise future returns. Education only, not financial advice.
Original story, characters and animation. Voices are AI.
